messages.subject: annotateWithGenicParts - Error in NSBS(i, x, exact = exact, strict.upper.bound = !allow.append,  :    subscript contains NAs
parts:
Hello all,

I am very new to NGS and especially BS. I have just started trying to use methylKit to analyze my data and now I am stuck and cannot figure out what is wrong.

I have gone through the entire example in the Vignette (using my own data) and I have a file with myDiff25p.hyper and myDiff25p.hypo, which look good, just as in the example. I downloaded an annotation of HG38 from UCSC in BED format as specified, but now I get this error when I use annotateWithGenicParts. Could you please explain what I'm missing here?

Input:
gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("RefSeqH38.bed.txt")
annotateWithGenicParts(myDiff25p.hypo,gene.obj)

Output:
> gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("RefSeqH38.bed.txt")
> annotateWithGenicParts(myDiff25p.hypo,gene.obj)
Error in NSBS(i, x, exact = exact, strict.upper.bound = !allow.append,  : 
  subscript contains NAs
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use
  suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)
2: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use
  suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)
3: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use
  suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)
4: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use
  suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)
5: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use
  suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)
6: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use
  suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)

Hopefully this makes sense to someone. If you need more info let me know, I'm not yet familiar enough with NGS and R that I know exactly which info you need. 

Thank you,
Freekje
